en: Price every service so each hour of a chair earns what it should
Margin per chair hour for every service
price, minutes, product cost and pay become the margin a service leaves for each hour of a chair, checked against a target for its category
a service that earns less per chair hour than the studio overhead is flagged red, with the margin left after overhead
minutes, product cost, pay model and the margin per hour you want give the price to charge, rounded as you like
current and new price, appointments and clients lost give the revenue and margin change and how many clients you can lose before the rise stops paying
the discount on visits you would have had anyway against the margin of the extra visits gives a net gain or loss before you start
price, no-show rate and late-cancel rate give the deposit to hold and the chair hours lost without it
planned minutes against real minutes by service and technician, with the margin lost on the extra time
prices of nearby studios for the same service with the gap to yours and who costs more
two services in one visit with the client saving, the minutes and the margin per chair hour
Price rise plan with monthly gain
each planned price with its start date, the new margin per hour and the monthly gain after the clients you expect to lose

Service menu with price, pay cost and margin per chair hour
One row per service: minutes, price, product cost, deposit and pay; margin and margin per chair hour (what a service leaves after product and pay for each hour of a chair) and the verdict fill in.

Appointments with price, cost, pay and margin
One row per appointment: technician, service, client, status, minutes, prices, discount, cost and pay; margin, new price and the offer prices used in messages fill in by themselves.

One row per price change: service, old and new price, reason and who made it; change percent, direction, margin change and the appointments of that month fill in.

Promotions with redemptions and cost per redemption
One row per promotion: kind, dates, discount percent, redemptions, revenue and discount given; the cost per redemption, the discount share, the days left and the status fill in by themselves.
Discount rules with the example price and the floor
One row per discount rule: category, percent off, who it applies to and the lowest price allowed; the average price, the example price, the margin left and the floor check fill in by themselves.

One row per combo of two services booked in one visit: minutes and price; the separate price, the client saving, the cost, the margin, the margin per chair hour and the verdict fill in by themselves.
Prices of nearby studios against ours
One row per nearby studio and service: its price, minutes and review score and the date you checked; our price, the gap, the gap percent and who costs more fill in by themselves.
Deposit rules with the amount kept on a no-show
One row per deposit rule: price from, deposit and the share kept on a no-show (a client who does not come and does not cancel) and on a late cancel; the amounts kept and the check fill in.

The owner, technicians, front desk and outside contacts with phone and pay model; a booth renter is a technician who rents a chair and keeps their own takings. This month fills in.
Seasons with demand factor and average revenue
